author: Anonymous (Amoraic compilation, Land of Israel)
ref: y. Hagigah 2:2, 77d (Krotoschin foliation; Lightfoot cites "Hieros. Chagigah, fol. 77. 4"). Sefaria "Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:2", segment 6 of 7 (1-based)
original: וַחֲמָא לְמִרְיָם בְּרַת עֲלֵי בְצָלִים. רִבִּי לָעְזָר בַּר יוֹסֵה אָמַר. תַּלְיָיא בְחִיטֵּי בִיזַיָיא. רִבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן חֲנִינָה אָמַר. צִירָא דְּתִרְעַא דְּגֵיהִנֹּם קְבִיעָ בְּאוּדְנָהּ. אֲמַר לוֹן. לָמָּה דָא כֵן. אָמְרִין לֵיהּ. דַּהֲוָות צַיְימָה וּמְפַרְסְִמָה. וְאִית דְּאָמְרֵי. דַּהֲוָות צַיְימָה חַד יוֹם וּמְקַזָּה לֵיהּ תְּרֵיי. אֲמַר לוֹן. עַד אֵימַת הִיא כֵן. אָמְרֵי לֵיהּ. עַד דְּיֵיתֵי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שֶׁטַח וַאֲנָן מְרִימִין לָהּ מִן גַּו אוּדְנָהּ וְקָבְעִין לֵיהּ גַּו אוּדְנֵיהּ.
original_edition: The Jerusalem Talmud, ed. Heinrich W. Guggenheimer (De Gruyter 1999–2015), Hebrew text as published on Sefaria (NLI). Hebrew as printed in the Guggenheimer text; cross-checked visually against the Gluck Hebrew PDF, printed p. 30 (same phrase). Vilna 1922 V4 djvu text used only as OCR confirmation.
english: He also saw Miriam, Onion-leaf’s daughter. Rebbi Eleazar bar Yose said, she was hanging on her breast nipples. Rebbi Yose ben Ḥanina said, the hinge of Hell’s door was fixed in her ear. He asked them, why? They told him, because she fasted and made herself famous. [Footnotes and the rest of the story omitted.]
translator: Heinrich W. Guggenheimer (English, as published on Sefaria)
page: printed p. 30 of the Gluck Hebrew PDF; Sefaria has no printed page
edition: Guggenheimer (De Gruyter 1999–2015) as on Sefaria; Gluck, Hebrew with commentary (archive.org JerusalemTalmudHagigah, CC BY-NC-ND 3.0), p. 30
what_it_says: In a legend set in the time of Simeon ben Shetah, Miriam daughter of Eli ("Onion-leaf") is seen in the afterlife with the hinge of Hell’s gate in her ear, punished for fasting and self-display; the passage does not mention Joseph, Heli, David or Jesus.
limits: The text does not mention Mary, Heli, genealogy or Davidic descent; the link to Mary is Lightfoot’s reading (see G3-03), not the Talmud’s. The epithet עלי בצלים is obscure and Guggenheimer renders it "Onion-leaf"; the Vilna and Gluck texts have "תלייא בחיטי ביזייא" where Lightfoot prints "בחוטי בזויא".

author: Anonymous (Amoraic compilation, Land of Israel)
ref: y. Sanhedrin 6:6 in Sefaria numbering (brief says 6:9 [6:6], 23c; the 23c folio was not checked). Sefaria "Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 6:6", segment 5 of 5 (1-based)
original: וַחַמָּא לְמִרְיָם בַּת עֲלֵי בְצָלִים תַּלְיָיא בְחִיטֵּי בִיזַיָיא. וְאִית דָּמְרִין. תִּירְעַת גֵּיהִנָּם קְבִיעָה גַּו אוּדְנָהּ. אֲמַר לוֹן. [לָמָּה. אָמְרִין לֵיהּ. בְּגִין דַּהֲוָת צַיְימָא וּמְפַרְסִיָיהּ לִמְגִי[רְ]תָהּ.
original_edition: The Jerusalem Talmud, ed. Heinrich W. Guggenheimer (De Gruyter 1999–2015), Hebrew text as published on Sefaria (NLI). Hebrew as printed in the Guggenheimer text; Gluck Hebrew PDF (Sanhedrin), PDF p. 45, checked by text layer only.
english: He also saw Miriam, Onion-leaf’s daughter, hanging on her breast nipples; but some say, the door of Hell was fixed in her ear. [He asked them, why? They told him, because she fasted and made herself famous among her neighbors. Some say, she fasted one day and was dissolute two days. He asked them] for how long? They told him, when Simeon ben Sheṭaḥ comes, we shall remove it from her ear and put is in his ear. [Footnotes omitted.]
translator: Heinrich W. Guggenheimer (English, as published on Sefaria)
page: PDF p. 45 of the Gluck Hebrew PDF (printed page not checked); Sefaria has no printed page
edition: Guggenheimer (De Gruyter 1999–2015) as on Sefaria; Gluck, Hebrew with commentary (archive.org TalmudofjerusalemSanhedrin, CC BY-NC-ND 3.0), p. 45
what_it_says: The Sanhedrin version repeats the same legend about Miriam daughter of Eli (ear and hell-gate motif, fasting, Simeon ben Shetah), again with no link to Mary, Davidic descent or Jesus.
limits: Same limits as G3-01. Sefaria 6:6 vs brief’s 6:9 not reconciled. Sefaria’s own page 6:9 is not this story; its English segments look misaligned with its Hebrew, so I did not rely on that page.

work: Horae Hebraicae et Talmudicae, vol. 3: Exercitations upon St. Luke
author: John Lightfoot (1602–1675)
date: 17th c.; Luke volume first published 1674 (archive.org title record); this printing Oxford 1859
ref: Lightfoot on Luke 3:23 "Which was the son of Heli", printed pp. 54–55; footnote h on p. 55 cites "Hieros. Chagigah, fol. 77. 4"
original: חמא מרים בת עלי בצלים. תליא בחוטי בזויא. צירא דתרעא דגיהנם קביע באודנה
original_edition: Hebrew as printed on the 1859 Oxford page image (PDF p. 61), read at 300 dpi; the third phrase read at lower resolution. Lightfoot prints "בחוטי בזויא", Sefaria/Vilna have "בחיטי ביזייא".
english: There is a discourse of a certain person who in his sleep saw the punishment of the damned. Amongst the rest [Hebrew: חמא מרים בת עלי בצלים]; which I would render thus, but shall willingly stand corrected if under a mistake; He saw Mary the daughter of Heli amongst the shades. R. Lazar Ben Josah saith, [Hebrew: תליא בחוטי בזויא] that she hung by the glandules of her breasts. R. Josah Bar Haninah saith, [Hebrew: צירא דתרעא דגיהנם קביע באודנה] that the great bar of hell’s gate hung at her ear. If this be the true rendering of the words, which I have reason to believe it is, then thus far, at least, it agrees with our evangelist, that Mary was the daughter of Heli: and questionless all the rest is added in reproach of the blessed Virgin, the mother of our Lord: whom they often vilify elsewhere under the name of Sardah.
translator: John Lightfoot (own rendering; English text of the 1859 Oxford printing)
page: printed p. 55, vol. 3 (running head "Ch. iii. 27.] Exercitations upon St. Luke")
edition: Horae Hebraicae et Talmudicae, vol. 3, Oxford University Press 1859 (archive.org horhebraicet03ligh); PDF 466 pp.
what_it_says: Lightfoot reads a Talmudic dream-vision as naming "Mary the daughter of Heli" and concludes that Luke 3:23 gives Mary’s line; this is the earliest documented proponent of that identification that I found.
limits: Lightfoot says he "would render thus" and would stand corrected. The quoted Hebrew is 13 words (below the 15-word minimum: Lightfoot prints only these fragments). The Heli link is his inference, not a Talmud statement. The 1674 date comes from the archive.org title only; the EEBO scan was not opened. Pre-1500 witnesses were not searched here.

author: Anonymous contributor
ref: Article MARY, sentence citing "Lightfoot (Hor. Talm., in loc.)"
english: This is confirmed by the passages adduced by Lightfoot (Hor. Talm., in loc.) from the Jewish writings, where Mary is expressly spoken of as the daughter of Heli.
page: page unknown (HTML transcription; the printed volume and page were not recorded)
edition: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 7th ed. (1842); read via jimclifford.ca transcription
what_it_says: The 1842 Britannica states that Lightfoot’s Jewish-writing passages expressly call Mary the daughter of Heli, and uses this to read Luke 3 as Mary’s descent.
limits: A secondary witness repeating Lightfoot; not an independent Talmud reading. Read from an HTML transcription, not a page scan.

author: Anonymous contributor
ref: Article MARY, sentence citing "Lightfoot (Hor. Talm. in loc.)"
english: This is confirmed by the passages adduced by Lightfoot (Hor. Talm. in loc.) from the Jewish writings, where Mary is expressly spoken of as the daughter of Heli.
edition: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 8th ed. (1860); read via jimclifford.ca transcription
what_it_says: The 1860 Britannica repeats the 1842 claim, again citing Lightfoot for the statement that Mary is called the daughter of Heli in Jewish writings.
limits: Same as G3-04: secondary, dependent on Lightfoot, transcription only.

author: Anonymous (Babylonian redaction)
ref: Bava Batra 109b, Sefaria segment 5 of 13 (1-based): Rava on Numbers 27:11
original: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ וְיָרַשׁ אֹתָהּ״; מִשְׁפַּחַת אָב קְרוּיָה ״מִשְׁפָּחָה״, מִשְׁפַּחַת אֵם אֵינָהּ קְרוּיָה ״מִשְׁפָּחָה״ – דִּכְתִיב: ״לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם״.
original_edition: Sefaria vocalized Aramaic (William Davidson Edition). Partial confirmation from Lublin 1576 Rashi/Tosafot djvu OCR (archive.org masekhetbavabatr00lubl): the phrase appears garbled as "דמשפתת אב קרויה משפחה".
english: Rava said in response that the verse states: “Then you shall give his inheritance to his kinsman who is next to him of his family, and he shall inherit it” (Numbers 27:11), emphasizing that “kinsman” is referring specifically to someone who is of his family, and it is the father’s family that is called one’s family, while one’s mother’s family is not called one’s family. Proof for this is found in another verse, as it is written: “By their families, by their fathers’ houses” (Numbers 1:2).
translator: William Davidson Edition (Sefaria), English and vocalized Hebrew/Aramaic; translator not named in the record
edition: William Davidson Edition (Sefaria); Lublin 1576 Rashi/Tosafot printing (OCR only, PDF 74 MB not downloaded)
what_it_says: Rava argues from Numbers 27:11 that only the father’s family is called "family" (mishpaḥah), while the mother’s family is not.
limits: The rule is stated in an inheritance context. The Gemara immediately objects from Judges 17:7 (a Levite described as "of the family of Judah") and treats the matter as difficult. The Lublin PDF was not downloaded (74 MB); the OCR is unreliable.

author: Anonymous (Babylonian redaction)
ref: Sanhedrin 19b, Sefaria segment 13 of 21 (1-based): R. Yehoshua ben Korḥa on II Samuel 21:8 (Michal raising Merab’s sons)
original: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב: ״אֶת חֲמֵשֶׁת בְּנֵי מִיכַל בַּת שָׁאוּל״? אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וְכִי מִיכַל יָלְדָה? וַהֲלֹא מֵירַב יָלְדָה! מֵירַב יָלְדָה וּמִיכַל גִּידְּלָה, לְפִיכָךְ נִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמָהּ. לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁכׇּל הַמְגַדֵּל יָתוֹם בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ יְלָדוֹ.
original_edition: Sefaria vocalized Aramaic (William Davidson Edition). No PD scan captured: the 1959 archive.org PDF returned 401 (restricted).
english: The Gemara asks: And according to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa as well, isn’t it written: “And the five sons of Michal, daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel” (II Samuel 21:8)? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa could have said to you to understand it this way: And did Michal give birth to these children? But didn’t Merab give birth to them for Adriel? Rather, Merab gave birth to them and died, and Michal raised them in her house. Therefore, the children were called by her name, to teach you that with regard to anyone who raises an orphan in his house, the verse ascribes him credit as if he gave birth to him.
translator: William Davidson Edition (Sefaria), English and vocalized Hebrew/Aramaic; translator not named in the record
what_it_says: The Talmud states that anyone who raises an orphan in his house is credited by scripture as if he had begotten him.
limits: This is a legal and ethical principle about raising an orphan, not a genealogical rule; it says nothing about the descent of Jesus, Joseph or Mary.

author: Anonymous (tannaitic, Land of Israel)
original: הָאוֹמֵר זֶה בְּנִי, נֶאֱמָן. זֶה אָחִי, אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן וְנוֹטֵל עִמּוֹ בְּחֶלְקוֹ. מֵת, יַחְזְרוּ נְכָסִים לִמְקוֹמָן.
original_edition: Sefaria Mishnah, Hebrew version Torat Emet 357 (vocalized).
english: One who says: This is my son, is deemed credible. One who says: This is my brother, is not deemed credible with regard to his other brothers’ obligation to share the inheritance with the subject of his statement.
translator: William Davidson Edition (Sefaria), English and vocalized Hebrew/Aramaic; translator not named in the record
edition: Sefaria Mishnah (Torat Emet 357); English William Davidson Edition
what_it_says: The Mishnah rules that a man who declares "this is my son" is believed, while a declaration of brotherhood is not.
limits: The rule governs claims among heirs to an estate, not genealogical lists. It does not address the Davidic line.

author: Anonymous (tannaitic)
original: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קִדּוּשִׁין וְאֵין עֲבֵרָה, הַוָּלָד הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַזָּכָר. וְאֵיזֶה, זוֹ כֹהֶנֶת, לְוִיָּה וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִית שֶׁנִּשְּׂאוּ לְכֹהֵן וּלְלֵוִי וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל. וְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קִדּוּשִׁין וְיֵשׁ עֲבֵרָה, הַוָּלָד הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַפָּגוּם.
original_edition: Sefaria Mishnah, Hebrew version Torat Emet 357 (vocalized).
english: There is a principle with regard to the hala-khot of lineage: Any case where there is betrothal, i.e., where the betrothal takes effect, and the marriage involves no transgression by Torah law, the lineage of the offspring follows the male, his father. And in which case is this applicable? For example, this is the case with regard to the daughter of a priest; or the daughter of a Levite; or the daughter of an Israelite, who married a priest, a Levite, or an Israelite. In all these cases the child’s lineage is established by his father’s family. And any case where there is a valid betrothal and yet there is a transgression, the offspring follows the flawed parent.
translator: William Davidson Edition (Sefaria), English and vocalized Hebrew/Aramaic; translator not named in the record
edition: Sefaria Mishnah (Torat Emet 357); English William Davidson Edition
what_it_says: Where a marriage is valid, the child’s lineage follows the father; where the marriage is forbidden, the child follows the flawed parent.
limits: The rule concerns priestly, Levitical and Israelite status (and mamzer rules). It does not mention the Davidic line or Mary, and it gives no rule for a case where the mother’s line is the only Davidic one.

author: traditional/anonymous
original: כֵּ֗ן בְּנ֣וֹת צְלׇפְחָד֮ דֹּבְרֹת֒ נָתֹ֨ן תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת נַחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֵ֣י אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וְהַֽעֲבַרְתָּ֛ אֶת־נַחֲלַ֥ת אֲבִיהֶ֖ן לָהֶֽן׃ וְאֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תְּדַבֵּ֣ר לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ כִּֽי־יָמ֗וּת וּבֵן֙ אֵ֣ין ל֔וֹ וְהַֽעֲבַרְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לְבִתּֽוֹ׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (Hebrew with cantillation, as on Sefaria; section markers removed)
english: “The plea of Zelophehad’s daughters is just: you should give them a hereditary holding among their father’s kinsmen; transfer their father’s share to them. Further, speak to the Israelite people as follows: ‘If a man dies without leaving a son, you shall transfer his property to his daughter.’” (27:7–8)
translator: JPS Tanakh, Gender-Sensitive Edition (English, via Sefaria)
edition: Sefaria, Miqra according to the Masorah and JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition
what_it_says: When a man dies without a son, his property passes to his daughter.
limits: Concerns land inheritance, not genealogy. The daughter inherits only when there is no son.

author: traditional/anonymous
ref: Numbers 36:6–8 (heiresses marry within the father’s tribe)
original: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה יְהֹוָ֗ה לִבְנ֤וֹת צְלׇפְחָד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֣ינָה לְנָשִׁ֑ים אַ֗ךְ לְמִשְׁפַּ֛חַת מַטֵּ֥ה אֲבִיהֶ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֥ינָה לְנָשִֽׁים׃ וְלֹֽא־תִסֹּ֤ב נַחֲלָה֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִמַּטֶּ֖ה אֶל־מַטֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י אִ֗ישׁ בְּנַחֲלַת֙ מַטֵּ֣ה אֲבֹתָ֔יו יִדְבְּק֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וְכׇל־בַּ֞ת יֹרֶ֣שֶׁת נַחֲלָ֗ה מִמַּטּוֹת֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ לְאֶחָ֗ד מִמִּשְׁפַּ֛חַת מַטֵּ֥ה אָבִ֖יהָ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לְאִשָּׁ֑ה לְמַ֗עַן יִֽירְשׁוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִ֖ישׁ נַחֲלַ֥ת אֲבֹתָֽיו׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (Hebrew with cantillation, as on Sefaria; section markers removed)
english: “This is what GOD has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: They may become the wives of anyone they wish, provided they marry into a clan of their father’s tribe.” (36:6) “Every daughter among the Israelite tribes who inherits a share must become the wife of someone from a clan of her father’s tribe, in order that every Israelite [heir] may keep an ancestral share.” (36:8)
translator: JPS Tanakh, Gender-Sensitive Edition (English, via Sefaria)
edition: Sefaria, Miqra according to the Masorah and JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition
what_it_says: Heiresses may marry anyone they wish, provided the husband comes from a clan of their father’s tribe, so that inheritance does not pass between tribes.
limits: Applies to heiresses of land and to tribal inheritance only; it gives no rule for genealogical reckoning or for a male line from the mother.

author: traditional/anonymous
original: וְלֹא־הָיָ֧ה לְשֵׁשָׁ֛ן בָּנִ֖ים כִּ֣י אִם־בָּנ֑וֹת וּלְשֵׁשָׁ֛ן עֶ֥בֶד מִצְרִ֖י וּשְׁמ֥וֹ יַרְחָֽע׃ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן שֵׁשָׁ֧ן אֶת־בִּתּ֛וֹ לְיַרְחָ֥ע עַבְדּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד ל֖וֹ אֶת־עַתָּֽי׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (Hebrew with cantillation, as on Sefaria; section markers removed)
english: Sheshan had no sons, only daughters; Sheshan had an Egyptian slave, whose name was Jarha. So Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to Jarha his slave; and she bore him Attai. (2:34–35)
translator: JPS Tanakh, Gender-Sensitive Edition (English, via Sefaria)
edition: Sefaria, Miqra according to the Masorah and JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition
what_it_says: Sheshan, who had no sons, gave his daughter to his Egyptian slave Jarha, and she bore Attai.
limits: The text does not state that Attai was reckoned as Sheshan’s son in the genealogy; I did not check commentaries on this reading.

author: traditional/anonymous
original: וּמִבְּנֵי֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים בְּנֵ֥י חֳבַיָּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י הַקּ֑וֹץ בְּנֵ֣י בַרְזִלַּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָ֠קַ֠ח מִבְּנ֞וֹת בַּרְזִלַּ֤י הַגִּלְעָדִי֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה וַיִּקָּרֵ֖א עַל־שְׁמָֽם׃ אֵ֗לֶּה בִּקְשׁ֧וּ כְתָבָ֛ם הַמִּתְיַחְשִׂ֖ים וְלֹ֣א נִמְצָ֑אוּ וַֽיְגֹאֲל֖וּ מִן־הַכְּהֻנָּֽה׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (Hebrew with cantillation, as on Sefaria; section markers removed)
english: Of the sons of the priests, the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Barzillai who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and had taken [their] name— (Ezra 2:61; Sefaria note: 'his' = Lit. 'their') ... these searched for their genealogical records, but they could not be found, so they were disqualified for the priesthood. (2:62)
translator: JPS Tanakh, Gender-Sensitive Edition (English, via Sefaria)
edition: Sefaria, Miqra according to the Masorah and JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition
what_it_says: Priests who married daughters of Barzillai took that wife’s family name; priests who could not find their genealogical records were disqualified from the priesthood.
limits: The name-taking is a family name, not a claim about the descent of the wife’s line; the case concerns priestly status. Nehemiah 7:63 was not separately quoted.

author: traditional/anonymous
original: כִּֽי־יֵשְׁב֨וּ אַחִ֜ים יַחְדָּ֗ו וּמֵ֨ת אַחַ֤ד מֵהֶם֙ וּבֵ֣ן אֵֽין־ל֔וֹ לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֧ה אֵֽשֶׁת־הַמֵּ֛ת הַח֖וּצָה לְאִ֣ישׁ זָ֑ר יְבָמָהּ֙ יָבֹ֣א עָלֶ֔יהָ וּלְקָחָ֥הּ ל֛וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֖ה וְיִבְּמָֽהּ׃ וְהָיָ֗ה הַבְּכוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּלֵ֔ד יָק֕וּם עַל־שֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו הַמֵּ֑ת וְלֹֽא־יִמָּחֶ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (Hebrew with cantillation, as on Sefaria; section markers removed)
english: When brothers dwell together and one of them dies and leaves no offspring, the wife of the deceased shall not be married to a stranger, outside the family. Her husband’s brother shall unite with her: he shall take her as his wife and perform the levir’s duty. (25:5) The first child that she bears shall be accounted to the dead brother, that his name may not be blotted out in Israel. (25:6)
translator: JPS Tanakh, Gender-Sensitive Edition (English, via Sefaria)
edition: Sefaria, Miqra according to the Masorah and JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition
what_it_says: In a levirate marriage the first son is accounted to the dead brother, so that his name is not blotted out in Israel.
limits: Applies only when brothers live together and the husband dies without a child. It is a rule about naming and inheritance, not a Gospel-type genealogy.

author: traditional/anonymous
ref: Ruth 4:10 (Boaz acquires Ruth as wife of the dead)
original: וְגַ֣ם אֶת־ר֣וּת הַמֹּאֲבִיָּה֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת מַחְל֜וֹן קָנִ֧יתִי לִ֣י לְאִשָּׁ֗ה לְהָקִ֤ים שֵׁם־הַמֵּת֙ עַל־נַ֣חֲלָת֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת שֵׁם־הַמֵּ֛ת מֵעִ֥ם אֶחָ֖יו וּמִשַּׁ֣עַר מְקוֹמ֑וֹ עֵדִ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (Hebrew with cantillation, as on Sefaria; section markers removed)
english: I am also acquiring Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, as my wife, so as to perpetuate the name of the deceased upon his estate, that the name of the deceased may not disappear from among his kinsmen and from the gate of his home town. You are witnesses today. (4:10)
translator: JPS Tanakh, Gender-Sensitive Edition (English, via Sefaria)
edition: Sefaria, Miqra according to the Masorah and JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition
what_it_says: Boaz acquires Ruth the Moabite as his wife so that the name of the dead man is kept upon his estate.
limits: Ruth is a Moabite; the JPS note on 4:6 says the child is "legally regarded as Mahlon’s", so the case is legal, not biological descent.

author: Jeremiah (traditional)
original: הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֔ה וַהֲקִמֹתִ֥י לְדָוִ֖ד צֶ֣מַח צַדִּ֑יק וּמָ֤לַךְ מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ וְהִשְׂכִּ֔יל וְעָשָׂ֛ה מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (Hebrew with cantillation, as on Sefaria; section markers removed)
english: See, a time is coming—declares GOD—when I will raise up a true branch of David’s line. He shall reign as king and shall prosper, and he shall do what is just and right in the land. (23:5)
translator: JPS Tanakh, Gender-Sensitive Edition (English, via Sefaria)
edition: Sefaria, Miqra according to the Masorah and JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive Edition
what_it_says: God promises to raise up a righteous branch for David who will reign.
limits: A prophetic oracle; it does not define how the "branch of David" is reckoned (paternal or maternal).

work: Mishneh Torah, Laws of Kings and Wars 11:1
author: Maimonides (Moses ben Maimon)
ref: Mishneh Torah, Kings and Wars 11:1 (first two sentences)
original: הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ עָתִיד לַעֲמֹד וּלְהַחְזִיר מַלכוּת דָּוִד לְיָשְׁנָהּ לַמֶּמְשָׁלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה. וּבוֹנֶה הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וּמְקַבֵּץ נִדְחֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
original_edition: Sefaria, Mishneh Torah Hebrew (Torat Emet 363, vocalized).
english: In the future, the Messianic king will arise and renew the Davidic dynasty, restoring it to its initial sovereignty. He will build the Temple and gather the dispersed of Israel.
translator: Eliyahu Touger (Mishneh Torah, Moznaim, via Sefaria)
edition: Mishneh Torah, Torat Emet 363 (Sefaria); Touger English
what_it_says: The Messianic king will arise and renew the Davidic dynasty in its initial sovereignty.
limits: Does not state whether descent must be through the father or the mother, or what proof of descent is required.

work: Talmud Yerushalmi, Tractate Hagigah, halakhah 2:2 (second segment)
author: Anonymous (Amoraic compilation, Land of Israel)
ref: y. Hagigah 2:2, halakhah; Sefaria segment 2 of 7 (1-based)
original: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה לֹא הָיְתָה מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא עַל הַסְּמִיכָה בִּלְבַד. וְעָמְדוּ שַׁמַּי וְהִלֵּל וְעָשׂוּ אוֹתָן אַרְבַּע. מִשֶּׁרָבוּ תַלְמִידֵי בֵית שַׁמַּי וְתַלְמִידֵי בֵית הִלֵּל וְלֹא שִׁימְשׁוּ אֶת רַבֵּיהֶן כָּל צוֹרְכָּן. וְרָבוּ הַמַּחֲלוֹקוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְנֶחְלְקוּ לִשְׁתֵּי כִּיתּוֹת. אֵילּוּ מְטַמְּאִין וָאֵילּוּ מַטַהֲרִין. וְעוֹד אֵינָהּ עֲתִידָה לַחֲזוֹר לִמְקוֹמָהּ עַד שֶׁיָּבוֹא בֶּן דָּוִד.
original_edition: The Jerusalem Talmud, ed. Heinrich W. Guggenheimer (De Gruyter 1999–2015), Hebrew text as published on Sefaria (NLI). Hebrew as printed in the Guggenheimer text. Also located on the Gluck Hebrew PDF, printed p. 29 (text layer: "עד שיבוא" ... "דוד").
english: Originally the only disagreement in Israel was about leaning on. Then rose Hillel and Shammai and made it four. [...] disagreements increased in Israel and they were split into two sects; these declare impure and those declare pure, and the prior state will not be reconstituted until the arrival of David’s son.
translator: Heinrich W. Guggenheimer (English, as published on Sefaria)
what_it_says: The Jerusalem Talmud says the prior state (ordination) will not be restored until the son of David comes.
limits: The clause refers to the institution of ordination (semikhah), not to a genealogy; it shows the expectation of a Davidic figure, not how that figure is reckoned.

work: Scholarship on the Talmudic Miriam daughter of Eli
what_it_says: Most modern scholars are said to treat the Talmudic Miriam daughter of Eli as a different woman from Mary of Nazareth.
limits: No source was read in this session. WebSearch returned only apologetic pages, old encyclopedias and one unopened article (Ezra Brand, "From Alexandria to Ashkelon") that a snippet describes as distinguishing a different Miriam.
memory_only: Most modern scholars do not identify the Talmudic Miriam daughter of Eli with Mary of Nazareth (from memory; not verified in this session).
